text: We conclude with a fictional subscription appointment-booking platform containing
a customer website mobile app admin dashboard and backend
A P I services Our fictional platform lets customers
register find appointments reserve a slot pay and receive
confirmation Staff use an administrative dashboard while a mobile
app and website share backend services A customer sees
one journey but the system contains several boundaries where
information can be delayed or misunderstood We will build
a connected testing plan across three illustrative sprints The
schedule is a teaching example not a requirement that
real teams deliver these exact features in separate sprints
Focus on how each increment adds evidence and how
earlier checks continue protecting behavior as the product grows
The backlog includes registration appointment discovery booking payments and
notifications Refinement uncovers risks involving duplicate bookings payment failures
cancellations and authorization Refine the journey before implementation A
reservation must belong to the requesting customer a slot
must not be confirmed for two people and a
payment outcome must update the booking consistently Ask when
temporary holds expire how cancellation affects availability and what
happens if a notification arrives late Identify dependencies among
identity availability and payment services Translate the highest risks
into examples that product development and testing participants can
understand This prevents the team from treating five attractive
screens as five independent features when their correctness actually
depends on shared state and coordinated outcomes
Developers implement registration and login Tests cover valid and
invalid input duplicate accounts password recovery and sessions Concurrent
registration exposes a race condition the team fixes and
retests it In the first sprint test registration and
login with synthetic accounts Check valid input rejected input
duplicate addresses recovery and session behavior Now send two
registration requests for the same address close together A
defect could allow duplicate accounts if the implementation checks
availability and creates the record as separate unprotected steps
Record the observed outcome discuss a safe implementation and
retest the fix Add an appropriate regression check The
important lesson is not a particular database command it
is that a realistic concurrency question can expose a
defect that sequential happy-path checks miss
Tests cover available slots unavailable slots simultaneous booking and
cancellation Integration tests protect against double booking Exploratory testing
identifies confusing messages and prompts an improvement In the
booking increment create one isolated appointment slot and two
customers Send competing reservation attempts Under the agreed rule
exactly one should succeed and the stored booking must
match the winning customer Check the response for the
unsuccessful customer and confirm that it offers an understandable
next step Cancel the successful reservation if the policy
permits it then verify whether availability returns as agreed
Also explore stale screens a customer may select a
slot that someone else reserved moments earlier The interface
and the backend must work together to handle that
change safely
Using a payment sandbox test success failure cancellation delayed
confirmation and duplicate callbacks A network timeout reveals incorrect
payment-state handling The team adds safe recovery and repeat-notification
checks For payments stay in the provider's sandbox Test
success decline user cancellation delayed confirmation and a repeated
callback Suppose the provider accepted payment but the platform
lost the response A retry should not create a
second charge or second booking Define the recovery policy
and examine how unique request identifiers and payment-state transitions
support it Verify records as well as the displayed
message A page saying Payment failed while the provider
recorded success is a serious inconsistency Capture the evidence
and add focused checks for the failure mode rather
than relying only on the standard successful purchase journey
Run regression checks across authentication booking and payments Evaluate
performance under concurrent searches authorization controls accessibility and resilience
Document remaining risks As new increments arrive rerun relevant
checks across identity booking and payment A permission change
in the dashboard could affect existing customer access A
payment-state fix could accidentally prevent cancellation Add nonfunctional questions
where the risks justify them concurrent search traffic keyboard
accessibility account isolation and recovery after a dependency failure
Use realistic synthetic data and record the tested conditions
No single green pipeline proves complete readiness Combine automated
results with exploratory findings unresolved defects and operational evidence
to explain what is known and what uncertainty remains
Review Definition of Done outstanding defects deployment and rollback
plans After release monitor logs failures and service health
Treat production feedback as another input to the quality
cycle Before release inspect the shared quality conditions open
risks deployment steps and recovery plan Make sure relevant
evidence belongs to the intended release candidate If a
serious unresolved payment issue remains either resolve it or
make an explicit scope and release decision with the
responsible stakeholders After deployment monitor error signals transaction consistency
and customer feedback using appropriate access controls A successful
deployment command is not the end of quality work
Production observations can reveal conditions that the test environment
did not reproduce and those observations should inform both
fixes and future checks
Your final exercise is to present a release recommendation
for this platform Name the three highest risks give
one piece of evidence for each and identify any
remaining uncertainty A strong response connects duplicate-registration checks competing-booking
results and payment-recovery verification to specific builds and conditions
It also explains how the team will detect problems
after release Look back at the whole course principles
guided priorities methods shaped examples artifacts preserved evidence tools
accelerated feedback and collaboration connected the work You now
have a practical way to discuss Agile Testing as
part of delivering a product from the first question
through production learning
Trace one defect across the entire case study A
repeated payment notification creates two booking confirmations Start by
reproducing the sequence with synthetic data in the sandbox
Link the failure to the rule that one successful
payment should confirm one reservation Investigate how event identifiers
and state transitions are handled After the fix repeat
the original sequence test a delayed notification and verify
that a distinct legitimate payment still works Retain the
build and results This evidence chain connects discovery implementation
and verification giving the release discussion more substance than
the statement that the ticket is now closed
Finally prepare a post-release learning loop Identify which signals
would reveal duplicate confirmations unusual payment failures or growing
booking errors Agree who reviews those signals and how
a new issue enters the team's work Use operational
data with the access and privacy controls appropriate to
the product When an incident occurs examine the contributing
conditions and improve both the product and the relevant
checks Production monitoring does not replace pre-release testing and
testing does not eliminate the need to observe a
live service Together they provide feedback across the product's
life and help the team adapt when real usage
reveals a new risk
Agile Testing begins with clear requirements and continues through
development integration exploration automation and production Quality is shared
across the team Congratulations on completing the masterclass Thank
you for completing the Agile Testing Masterclass with Tech

approach to a small feature and share your most
